To investigate the formation of the Al/Hf/Ta rich phase, several single bead samples were fabricated, as shown in Fig. 2 . These single beads were fabricated on an L-PBF built cube with a flat top surface to ensure that the conditions were consistent.

The tensile test samples were machined from Φ 10 mm × 60 mm rods built at both vertical and horizontal directions. They underwent hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1260 ∘ C, 150 Mpa for 2 h, followed by solution treated at 1260 ∘ C for 2 h, then aged at 980 ∘ C for 5 h, and 870 ∘ C for 20 h.

Fig. 1f of the high E L large hatch samples shows misorientated columnar dendrites growing from melt pool boundary to the melt pool centre, while the columnar grains grow vertically near the melt pool center line.
Fig.2c demonstrates clear misoriented columnar dendrites at the edge and vertical columnar dendrites at the center.

The EBSD results in Fig. 3b shows that the sample exhibits a strong 〈 001 〉 texture columnar grain along the building direction, but misoriented columnar grains with a random texture are observed in the Al/Hf/Ta rich phase area.
Serval cracks are found at the boundary between the 〈 001 〉 columnar grain and 〈 101 〉 grain, indicating misorientation is a critical factor for grain boundary cracking in CM247LC superalloys.

These phases represent the primary surface segregation in L-PBFed Ni-superalloys, which has Al:(Hf + Ta) ratio higher Al 3 Hf, indicating these are α -Al + Al 3 Hf compound instead of the widely reported γ - γ ′ eutectic or MC phase
Subsequently, the primary segregation oxidise to Al 2 O 3 + Ta(Hf)O 2 phase during solidification.
Fig. 5d shows the tensile sample has fine cubic γ ′ with around 0.4 μ m size after HT.
Large size redistributed segregation oxide is difficult to be melt, thus remain in the sample as unmelt segregation oxide.
The primary segregation oxide, which arises through segregation channels between misoriented dendrites, exhibits a bubble- shaped morphology on the melt pool surface.
During the remelting of the subsequent scan pass, it is redistributed along the melt boundary by laser depression and Marangoni flow, adopting a line-shaped morphology.
In contrast, the high power sample exhibited a large amount of redistributed segregation, misorientated columnar grains and unmelted segregations as depicted in Fig. 5b .
This study reports, for the first time, an Al/Hf/Ta rich segregation in L-PBFed Ni-superalloys, which significantly impacts mechanical performance at elevated temperatures.

Consequently, the growing direction of the secondary dendrites is no longer parallel to the melt pool surface, creating an escape channel along 〈 111 〉 or 〈 110 〉 directions for the grain boundary elements to flow towards the melt pool surface.
